reason: New entry, read in full on 2026-11-12 (the source, the built sidecar dist/spec/evals-baseline/1.0.md and dist/spec/evals-baseline/1.0.html, clean build of the working tree). It holds the sections docs/plan/reference/evals-baseline-spec.md 8.1 lists: terms (2.1), rules 1 to 4 and the binding check (2.2, 2.4), the finding and note vocabulary (2.5), exit codes (5.2), the baseline schema (3.1, 3.2), value, sample count and metric key per tool shape (6.2, 6.3), the three properties (10), the permanent refusals (11), the versioning policy (8.2) and a changelog. Checked by script against the design document: 103 of the 105 backticked identifiers, field names, message texts and finding ids are verbatim in it, and so are the baseline example and the DeepEval verdict message. The example is a bare pre block and the message an inline code span, because the fenced-code renderer of the site, expressive-code, emits markup that the html-validate gate of the site rejects. The two others are the rule 3 note text (the design writes note: outside the code span, same words, with a printed example at its line 410) and results.prompts[i].metrics, a parent path the design's tables leave implicit (metrics.namedScores[m]) and the sibling implementation reads at that path. Table prose is paraphrased from the design, never quoted, and no usage, install or invocation text from the README half is restated. The versioning section reconciles the design's PATCH row with the two-number address of L77 and section 8.4: an editorial correction changes no behaviour and no citation and is dated in the changelog, and any change of behaviour is a new version at its own address. L76 holds: no repository, GitHub or npm address and no claim that a repository exists; the single external link is RFC 2119 with rel nofollow noopener noreferrer. The citeAs template is the paste-ready sentence of section 8.4. Three passages were then written by the integrator on 2026-11-12 and read in the same build. The summary-line clause of the printed-lines section was added, because conformance is defined as reproducing the expected output and the summary line is part of it; it states the four forms, the fourth of which exists because every finding is `cases-changed` and no finding can change the exit code. The cited address lost its trailing slash, because the site is built with `trailingSlash: 'never'` and the slash form answers with a 308, so the page printed two forms of one address. The versioning paragraph was split in three and the summary clause into a list, because the first ran to 92 words and the second to a 48-word sentence, over the limits `gate:content` and `gate:human` hold. The JSON example of the baseline file became a fenced block: it was written as raw `<pre>` markup, which reached the sidecar and `/llms/spec.txt` as HTML tags, and which axe reported on the narrow viewport as a region that scrolls and no keyboard can reach. Prettier then rewrapped the file on 2026-11-12, which changed line breaks and no words. The conformance-vectors section was rewritten on 2026-11-12 when the vectors were published, and read in dist/spec/evals-baseline/1.0.html and in the sidecar. It says an implementation conforms when it reproduces every vector that is not marked reference-only, links the vectors file at /spec/evals-baseline/1.0/vectors.json and the baseline schema at /spec/evals-baseline/1.0/baseline.schema.json, and says that the vectors file carries, under the key files, the exact text of every baseline file and run file that a vector names and that exists, so that the file alone is enough to run every vector. That sentence is held to the file: site/src/data/spec-vectors.site.test.mjs fails when it and the vectors file disagree. Every number in the section is recomputed from the vectors file by that test, which also fails when a table row, a total or a sentence drifts and prints what to paste; 165, 116, 57, 22, 18, 49, 67, 102 and 4000000000 are in the numbers list of site/content-facts.json so `gate:content` holds them to a source. The sentence under the coverage table was corrected twice. It first claimed the rows total more than the vectors that produce them, which ran the wrong way, and it then said 21 vectors name no finding, which none of the counts measured from the file gives. What is true, measured from the file: a vector stands in a row for each finding its report names, 4 name two findings and stand in two rows, 67 of the 165 name no finding and stand in no row, and of those 67, 18 are check runs that must stay silent while the other 49 are the record, show, version and usage vectors, which report no finding. The rows total 102, which is 165 minus 67 plus 4, and the test asserts that sum and that no vector names more than two findings. A sentence in the baseline-file section links the JSON Schema and says it checks the shape only. The schema is held by site/src/data/spec-baseline-schema.site.test.mjs, which validates the page's own example and every baseline that a record vector writes against it, refuses each broken variant the test lists and accepts the variants a reader accepts, and by site/src/data/spec-baseline-inputs.site.test.mjs, which validates each baseline file that the vectors file carries as an input and requires the schema to accept exactly the ones that no vector refuses, except one whose key repeats, which only a scanner can see. That test found that the schema had no bound on a metric value while the reference reader refuses a value of more than 4000000000 in size, and the schema now carries the bound. Two statements on the page were added for the same reason, because the vectors test them and the page did not say them: the list of reasons for refusing a baseline names a key that appears twice in one object, and the field table gives the range of the value, from -4000000000 to 4000000000, and of the tolerance, from 0 to 4000000000. They were read on 2026-11-12 against src/quantise.mjs, where largestQuantisable is 4000000000 and the test is that the size of the value is at most that, and against src/unreadable.mjs, which refuses a key that appears twice in one object, and against the vectors S16-baseline-value-4000000001 and S16-baseline-duplicate-metric, which a reader must refuse as bad-baseline. Both files are served from copies in site/src/data/spec/evals-baseline-1.0/, and the vectors copy is byte for byte the reference implementation's vectors file, which mirror.json in that folder checks on a machine that has the checkout. After the reference implementation changed and its vectors grew from 108 to 165, the page was corrected on 2026-11-12 from the implementation and the vectors, not from the design document, so the check against the design document above does not cover these passages and none of them is quoted from it. Rule 2 defines q as floor(x * 1,000,000 + 0.5) in double-precision arithmetic. The values section gives the range of a value, the order of the sum and the mean, the value as q(mean) divided by 1,000,000, and a table of means at or near a tie with the value each vector prints. The Sorted term fixes UTF-16 code-unit order. The digest clauses fix the canonical form and the first result of a repeated test index. The printed-lines section lists the escaped characters, the line starts, the order of lines, the four summary forms with the plural rule, the four texts that print (s) as written, the banner and the form of a number. The vectors are named the normative annex for exact text, except those marked reference-only. The clauses on reading, recording and exit codes state which spec forms are refused, that a repeated key in a run is refused, what record refuses, that a record whose only differences are the date and the tool version writes nothing, and that every report goes to standard output except a usage error. The coverage table gained a column that counts the vectors to reproduce, and says that internal-error has none. Each statement was read on 2026-11-12 against the relevant parts of the reference sources src/quantise.mjs, src/command.mjs, src/compare.mjs, src/render.mjs, src/record.mjs, src/read-run.mjs, src/read-baseline.mjs, src/unreadable.mjs and src/digest.mjs, and against the vectors in the published file. The statements that the vectors can test are held by site/src/data/spec-values.site.test.mjs and site/src/data/spec-printed-forms.site.test.mjs, which were run red against the page before these corrections, and by site/src/data/spec-vectors.site.test.mjs, which also holds the new column. The second changelog row, which had called the publication of the vectors an editorial correction, was removed: the page is not on origin/main, so no earlier text of version 1.0 was ever public, and the changelog holds the one row First publication. G92 is closed and G93 is partly closed by this change.
